interface_debt.quote: uint32 Seconds; /**< \brief Number of seconds since epoch
interface_debt.why: Users can read and write Seconds and Subseconds directly, so the public time value is a frozen two-uint32 layout. If cFE later changes the representation to 64-bit seconds, a different subsecond unit, signed time, or added fields, every user that touches these members must change source and layout assumptions.
interface_debt.better: Expose time through an opaque or private representation with accessors and arithmetic functions, rather than making the internal Seconds/Subseconds fields part of the public API.

interface_debt.quote: define CFE_TIME_PRINTED_STRING_SIZE 24 /**< \brief Required size of buffer to be passed into #CFE_TIME_Print (includes null terminator)
interface_debt.why: The macro freezes the required printed-time buffer size at 24 bytes. If cFE later prints a longer or different time string, such as more precision, a leap-second indicator, negative time, or timezone information, users who allocate fixed buffers from this constant must change their buffers and any derived layout.
interface_debt.better: Provide a function that returns the required size for a given time, or make CFE_TIME_Print take a buffer size and report the needed size, so the printed format can evolve without a fixed public constant.
